mechanics.textEn: The boss flies to the middle and four rocks appear at the edges. While he casts, everyone hides behind a rock — the green area behind each one is safe. Anyone left in the open is one-shot. Watch his cast bar.
mechanics.legendEn: Boss in the middle, four rocks at the edge; stand in the green shadow behind a rock.

mechanics.textEn: After a pizza-slice hit, bright sparks flash around him and he spins after one player, adding bleeding. Stay out of his path; new players can burn a dodge, a potion or an invulnerability here.
When he raises his claws a stagger bar appears — break it fast or the group dies. Save your stagger skills for this moment; a broken bar stuns him for a few seconds of free damage.

The screen goes black and everyone lands at the edge on opposite sides. Waves roll out from the boss: run in at once and jump each wave (Space) to reach the safe zone right next to him — gap-closers of Gladiator, Chanter and Assassin help. Then break the stun bar immediately: a slow group runs out of time and wipes.
mechanics.legendEn: Start at the edge, jump the rings, finish next to the boss.

mechanics.textEn: He dives and attacks every player separately — keep moving and spread out. A big area hit ends the phase: just get out of it. Near the end the wave phase repeats with tornadoes on the water to run around.
His winds hit in front of him — stand behind. If they catch you, he lifts you in his beak for a few seconds and slams you into the ground.

He flies up, marks one player with his eye and a small field grows around them, with arrows pointing in from four sides. Everyone runs into that circle and splits the final hit, or the marked player dies. Avoid the wind lines on the way. In the second phase he does the same from the middle, with a vortex around the arena.
mechanics.legendEn: Arrows from four sides: the whole group stacks inside the marked circle.

mechanics.textEn: She retreats to the middle and poisons everything but a small circle around her; a flower blooms inside — kill it to clean the area. She throws poison at every player and it stays on the ground, so the whole group moves together in one direction to keep a clean patch.
mechanics.legendEn: Kill the flower; move together so the poison stays behind you.

mechanics.textEn: Light circles flash under the players; stay in one and you turn to stone. The others break the stone fast, because a huge area hit comes right after and hits whoever is still trapped.
In the second phase he puts a vampiric buff on himself: red glow — melee stops hitting; purple glow — casters stop. Hitting into the wrong colour heals him a lot.

He throws a seed at a player; a few seconds later it roots them in spikes with heavy damage over time and spreads to anyone close. The seeded player steps out of the group — not too far, so the others can still hit the spikes and free them.

mechanics.nameEn: Red floor: three waves and a blast
mechanics.textEn: The whole floor turns red. Three waves roll out from him — jump each one. At the same time attacks shoot out of the centre along lines in every direction, in two sets that take turns: stand between the lines of the next set. A moment after the third wave a blast covers the area: dodge it with a jump too. The easy way: on the third wave jump, press Space again and glide, and the blast passes under you.
mechanics.legendEn: Jump the three rings; the red lines are the attacks from the centre — stand between them; glide over the final blast.

mechanics.textEn: He goes to the middle and pulls everyone in; rocks grow around him and one is reddish. The whole group breaks that rock and runs out of the circle through the gap — if it stays, everyone dies.
mechanics.legendEn: Break the red rock, leave the circle through its gap.

mechanics.textEn: Bow raised: arrows rain on every player — keep moving. Bow lowered: balls fly out in several directions and debuff whoever they hit. Then she leaps from player to player with area hits, and later a three-stage leap whose radius grows each time.

She flies up and walls of fire sweep across the arena with one safe window each. The windows jump left and right, so turn early — with high ping, start turning before you reach the wall. Heal and use invulnerabilities; surviving is all that matters. The second time, fireballs fly around the arena too.
mechanics.legendEn: One window per wall, never in the same place: zigzag through.

mechanics.textEn: She moves to the middle and illusions appear that attack fast, then close in and hit an area together — dash or run out of it. After the second fire walls more illusions shoot fire arrows from the edges.

He jumps onto his statue, marks and roots a player and his illusion jumps away from them while a circle grows. Read the arrows: small circle — the supports run in; large circle — they run out. One more player stands in the illusion's path, or its damage-taken debuff kills the marked player when the wolf lands. Two jumps the first time, three the second.

mechanics.nameEn: Redirect the strike into the orb
mechanics.textEn: He casts an orb in the middle that pulls players slightly, jumps to the side and marks a player. The marked player runs to the opposite side, through the area hits, so his ranged strike passes through the orb. Three hits out of four attempts must go into the orb; he jumps somewhere new every time.
mechanics.legendEn: Boss, orb and marked player on one line.

mechanics.textEn: His whip hits hurt on weak gear; a debuff that reaches three stacks makes you explode with lightning in all directions. He marks a player and charges twice, leaving an electric puddle each time — the marked player drags him to a corner so the puddles don't cover the arena. Then he pounds the ground from the middle: dodge the zones before the big whip hit.
A large ring appears and he swings the great whip in every direction for colossal damage — run out of the ring or block it with skills.

She pulls the group together and a thread links the players — run apart to break it. Then she roots a player: everyone runs into that circle to share the damage. Waves fly out that hurt and stun briefly — find their rhythm — while a wind pushes you to the edge, which explodes and shrinks at the end.

Copies rush across the arena like a train while a red thread punishes going too far from her. Then she spawns a stagger bar, but the wind blows melee off — close in with skills and break it while dodging her pizza hits. If the bar holds, the run fails.

First she throws rings at a few players, then the rest fly out — read their path to find a safe spot. The main mechanic is for two players: two rings slowly come at them along red bars. Stand so the bars form a cross and the rings collide. If one player moves at the last second they fly past and must be lined up again; a failed try sends them after you and hurts everyone. Adjust calmly.
mechanics.legendEn: Two players make the red bars cross; the rings meet in the middle.

mechanics.textEn: Four spears appear, three purple and one white — attack the white one or it hits very hard. Circles on the water mean fire beams from above that move chaotically. She sends a white wave outward and a purple wave inward: jump both.

Purple and white orbs converge on her from all sides — agree in advance who collects which colour; each missed orb raises her damage. When they run out a dome of your colour forms over you; don't stand close to others or the domes vanish. Remember the order of colours she shows: everyone stands under the dome of the first colour, then moves to the second. The second time there are three colours and waves to jump.
mechanics.legendEn: Each player under their own dome, apart; go to the colour she shows first.

mechanics.textEn: She locks one player in a cage that takes damage and throws spears at the other three, their path shown by a yellow bar. Aim all three at the cage: three hits shatter it.
Dodge everything: single hits and short combos all hurt, and they bleed — clear it with potions or skills. One attack tethers and lifts you, then his huge sword lands.

He jumps to the edge and slams the ground; once he has struck, a safe lane forms — step in, never before. He reappears on the opposite side and slams a second, roughly parallel lane: start moving when the purple glow fades, not earlier and not later. If you are outside a lane when the arena lights purple again, you die. Then he dives to the middle — jump right before the landing wave. The second round adds area hits on the floor and a third side; at the end the safe spot is right next to him.
mechanics.legendEn: He strikes from one side, then the other: move from lane to lane on his swing.

options.textEn: Macro bind a key — usually the right mouse button It has no key by default, and without one the in-game macro simply does not work.
Separate Defiance Hotkey ON + its own key On Space, Defiance shares a key with jump and glide — mash it under control and you take off gliding.
Fly Up, Fly Down comfortable keys The defaults are Ctrl+R and Ctrl+F, and you need both all the time.
Interact a second key : F + Z Tap the two in turn — quest dialogues skip much faster.
Auto-use → Buff Auto-use Conditions In Combat Buff scrolls stop burning while you run around town.
Controls → Skill Queue ON The macro works best with it.
Target Scanning → Preferred Search Direction Front of Camera Tab takes the target you are looking at.
Target Scanning → Detailed Settings Priority Ranking , Hostile Players first For PvP: Tab takes players before mobs.
Aggro Range Display ON You see where a mob will aggro.
Display Boss Orientation Indicator ALL You see where the boss's back is.
Effect Quality Very Low The biggest FPS gain and far less flashing on screen.
Player Particle Effect Display Self Only Hides everyone else's skill effects.
Identical Player Appearance, [Abyss] Display as Tier Icon ON A must for mass PvP.
Teleport Effect Color Dark No white flash on every teleport.
Camera Shake Effect During Combat OFF No shaking in combat.
World Map Transition Animation OFF No animation every time you open the map.
Control Mode AION 2 Better for the macro on a mouse button; see above.
Display Distance to Aimed Target ON Shows the distance to the target above its nameplate.
Adjust Aim Position to taste Moves the aim up or down on the screen (188px in the video).
Select Aimable Target Hostile Target Otherwise the aim also picks allies. You rarely need to target an ally — it is better to stay on the one you are attacking.
Pursue Targets with Skill Activation OFF for ranged, optional for melee When ON, pressing a skill out of range makes the character walk to the target and then use it. OFF gives more control.

Auto Target Upon Skill Use ON for open-world farming (default: OFF) With no target selected, a skill picks the nearest one: run around holding the macro and it goes from mob to mob. Grobs always turns it on for farming, above all on ranged classes; Whelps keeps it off outside farming.
Set Main Target Upon Attack two ways, see below (default: ON, both clicks ON) Whether an attack locks the target. Whelps: ON with left click ON and right click OFF. Grobs: OFF on melee.
Skill Queue ON A skill pressed during another one is queued. Gives the best result with the macro.
Preferred Search Direction Front of Camera (default: None) Tab looks for targets where the camera points, so you control what it picks.

Target Scanning Detailed Settings Priority Ranking (default: Closest First) If you PvP: targets are picked by your own priority list instead of by distance. In the Abyss there are mobs and players side by side — Tab must take the player.

Looting → Obtaining Gear / Obtaining Item All, or filter You can stop picking up a gear grade (Common, Rare …) or an item type (potions, shards, crafting materials) — useful when the bag fills up on a farm.
Auto-use → Buff Auto-use Conditions In Combat Buff scrolls usually sit on auto-use. With the «in motion» option they are used the moment you move, with «always» — all the time. Both waste scrolls.
Auto-use → Life Potion ON , 83% in the video Potions are drunk automatically below the chosen HP.

General → Separate Defiance Hotkey + Set Defiance Hotkey ON , key ` (left of 1); default: OFF By default Defiance (breaks control) is on Space together with jump and glide. Spam Space under control — and you start gliding, which ruins your next move: a boss mechanic or a PvP fight is lost.

General → Fly Up, Fly Down side mouse button for Fly Up; defaults: Ctrl+R and Ctrl+F Flies straight up or down without tilting the camera — in PvP the camera stays on the target. You need both all the time, and nobody presses Ctrl+R for that: rebind them on the first login and get used to them.

General → Macro right mouse button; default: no key Without a key the macro does not work at all. It is held down all fight, so it goes on the most comfortable button — for most players the right click.

General → Target Hostile Players Caps (Whelps); e.g. the middle mouse button (Grobs) Targets enemy players only. In the Abyss Tab keeps landing on mobs — this key does not. Grobs does not use it himself: for him Priority Ranking is enough.
General → Switch Control Mode / Switches between the AION 2 and AION 1 modes on the fly.
General → Combat Analysis Ctrl+X Opens the built-in damage meter.
Menu → Display Cursor Alt (hold) In AION 2 mode: hold it to get the cursor and click the interface.
Quickslot two keys per slot Every hotbar slot takes a main and a second key.
Marker numpad sets a marker, Ctrl+1 selects marker 1 For group PvP with voice chat: the leader marks a target, everyone selects it with one key.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Combat → Aggro Range Display ON Select a monster and you see a blue circle — step inside and it attacks.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Combat → Display Boss Orientation Indicator ALL An arc around the boss: the blue part is its front, the yellow one its back. Helps to stand behind it.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Combat → Display Skill Range ON Shows the range of your skills.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Common → Performance → Display Network Status ON A ping indicator in the corner of the screen.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Common → Pets → Display Other Players' Pets OFF Your own pet stays, everyone else's disappear — they only cost performance.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Common → Nameplate to taste Hide the nameplates of other players, their spirits and monsters to clear the screen. Your own nameplate cannot be hidden.

options.group: Info Display: what is shown on screen
options.textEn: Floater → Combat Floater Display ON, with a smaller UI The flying damage and healing numbers. They can be turned off, all or one by one (damage on me, heal on me, damage on target …), but then hits feel empty. Grobs keeps them and makes them smaller with UI Proportion — see Graphics.

settingsGroups.titleEn: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: UI Proportion Small (default: Medium) Scales the interface and the damage numbers together: a smaller UI means smaller numbers, so they stop covering the fight.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: Effect Quality Very Low Hits FPS harder than anything else (Whelps keeps the rest on Very High) and removes a lot of particles — much easier on the eyes over long sessions.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: Upscaler DLSS On an NVIDIA card.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: Frame Generator off in PvE , on for mass PvP Frame generation adds input lag, and input lag is lost damage. In big fights smoothness matters more.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: Player Particle Effect Display Self Only (Grobs); Self and Party (Whelps) Self Only hides the skill effects of everyone else, teammates included: less clutter and a clear FPS gain. You will notice it is missing now and then — worth it.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: NVIDIA Reflex BOOST Lower input delay.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: Volumetric Light Scattering, Volumetric Fog OFF in the video Set on his screen; he does not comment on them.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: [Abyss] Display as Tier Icon ON Enemy nameplates in the Abyss turn into small rank icons — far fewer labels on screen.

options.group: Graphics → Optimize: FPS and mass PvP
options.textEn: Identical Player Appearance ON All other players get the same simple look; applies at once. The game is not optimized for sieges and other large-scale fights — without this they are close to unplayable on any PC.
World Map Transition Animation OFF Otherwise an animation plays every time you open the map — it gets dizzying.
Teleport Effect Color Dark (default: Bright) The bright version is a white screen in your face on every teleport.
Camera Perspective Default, or over the shoulder The second option puts the character slightly left of the centre.
Camera Shake Effect During Combat OFF Both authors turn it off. A matter of taste — some like the shaking.
Display Weapon Outside of Combat ON (default: OFF) Purely for looks: the weapon stays visible instead of disappearing outside combat.
Display Equipped Title Effects on Nameplate to taste The frames of special titles around names. OFF removes them; there is also «on my nameplate only».

progressionSections.leadEn: From the datamine of the global client. This is why the Korean route no longer works as is.
bullets: Enemy ? marks lost the Daevanion crystals — they used to be the top goal at launch; now clear them at your own pace.
Feathers ([trace]) are nerfed — collect them all, but last.
Gear has a lower item level on global (for example True Dragon Lord Greatsword: 70 on KR/TW, 62 on global) — lower item level means cheaper enhancement.

progressionSections.titleEn: Story, regional quests and your map
bullets: 💡 TIP: Milestones. You reach 45 at about 700 item level. The last step of the main story (in the Abyss) asks for about 1,000 — if it doesn't let you in, do the steps below first and come back: Daevanion crystals, clash runes, belt and amulet, Exploration: Draupnir.

Finish the main story first. It gives a gold weapon for your class, [bracelet] and [wings] (equipped: HP 500, MP 250, Penetration 500, Critical Hit 35; owned: Penetration 100, Accuracy +20, Attack +10).
Regional quests (Journal → Regional): two rings, two earrings and a necklace (blue), plus two PvE runes. They also give titles and Theostone chests.
Enhance a little, set up your PvE macro and clear every ? on your own map: each sealed dungeon gives [dcrystal] ×2 and 2 skill points, each stronghold [beltscroll] ×2.
Then the remaining regional quests and the feathers: at least 95 [trace] take the Monolith to level 11, which upgrades the amulet from green to blue.

Clash runes ([clashrune]): 60 item level each, so the pair is +120. They come from green quests around the map, or buy them in the Nightmare shop (Growth tab) with the currency from first clears. Don't enhance them past +1 unless you have a spare.

The story bracelet ([bracelet]) stays with you for months: take it to +10–11 — it adds attack and defense too — and put your one [mana_sup] in it: two gold rolls give the most item level. The second bracelet comes from a quest of your own faction (item level 43).

progressionSections.leadEn: Without the enemy ? marks you end up around 1,279 — about 121 short of the 1,400 needed for the tier 2 dungeons. This is how to close the gap.
bullets: Mini-games with a reward card at the end. Your place decides how many cards you open. If you placed badly you can skip the reward — the [shugokey] is only spent when you take it. Keys: 7 by default, +1 a day, up to 30 more stored — don't let them cap.

Boss rifts (e.g. Beritra Air Raid): hold off the waves, then kill the mini-boss. 100 contribution points = 3 cards, the same rewards as Shugo. Invite Chanters, Clerics and Templars right at the portal — their party buffs make 100 points easy.

💡 TIP: The main prize is Shugo currency: spend all of it on [dcrystal] in the Festival Shop — per character, price goes up in steps: 50 (×10), 100 (×10), 200 (×15), 400 (×15) — [shugocoin] ×10,500 in total.

Solo boss dungeon. 14 base attempts that refill on their own (+2 a day), plus a second pool of up to 30 that you fill with tickets; charges start piling up at level 45 — reach it before the first reset.
Every boss has 10 challenge levels; kill each on all of them. An attempt is spent only on a kill, so leave and come back stronger. Greys first, then greens, then the Last Boss.
First clear gives [nmcoin] ×500, repeats 100. Shop, Growth tab: [dcrystal] for 300 (×50 per character), [stigmashard] for 1,500 (×35), [clashrune] for 500. Keep 14,000 for the statue.

Run it up to the guarantee: 14 chest openings (7 with premium), 40 Odyle energy each. The goal is two gold pieces from drops and a third from the guarantee — you pick which Bakarma piece ([bakarma], helm, pauldrons, gloves, greaves, boots).
Collect every [trace] in Chaotic Lower Reshanta: the Monolith resonance levels give Daevanion crystals such as [dcrystal_azphel].
Still short? Three runs of Exploration: Draupnir guarantee another gold piece — take any you don't have and put an [mana_int] in it.
Plus a green Theostone in the weapon (for example [theostone]) — the regional quests hand one out. Done right, that is exactly 1,400.

Belt and amulet: green → blue in Substance Morph, then up to gold — a big jump in item level. Enhancing them eats enhancement stones: the enemy ? marks (through the Rift, every 3 hours) give 2,500 [enhance] each — see the table at the top.

Spend Odyle energy with care: after each new piece enhance it, add manastones, check your item level, and only then decide where to go next — another run of the same dungeon or something you haven't done yet.
Farm Vakron Sky Island (2–5 players, 40 energy a chest) until you have almost the whole armor set. Weapon and accessories are best crafted later, so Urugugu Canyon (weapon, accessories) can wait.
[vakronguard] has no real alternative early. If it doesn't drop: every 21st chest gives [voucher]; two of them + 1,500,000 kina make the guard in Substance Morph.
Take the set to +10. If you bought every Daevanion crystal, you should be around 1,900. Short? Manastones, or one run on each boss of ★1 Transcendence — grey arcana add about 40.

Run ★2 Transcendence until you have the two green slots — bell and mirror ([bell_green], [mirror_green], item level 40 each). Fill the other slots with grey arcana ([compass_grey], [chalice_grey] — item level 20). Bonuses don't matter yet, only item level.
Transcendence opens at 1,600. Five arcana slots: a grey card gives 20 item level, green 40, blue 60. A full green set is +200 (1,600 → 1,800), swapping it for blue is another +100.
Go straight to Ferocious Horn Den (the RU community calls it “the Dog”) and stay until you have most of its armor set. Move your Vakron enhancement into the new pieces with Gear Transfer.
Fire Temple, the other dungeon of this tier, drops the weapon and accessories.

progressionSections.titleEn: To 2,800: gold arcana and the raid
bullets: Farm gold arcana in ★4 Transcendence and roll the skills you need for your PvE and PvP setups (for example [mirror_gold] +5 with the Primal Vigor set). At 2,800 the 10-player dragon raid opens — the hardest PvE of Season 1 and a source of resources for the next update.

From here +10–11 is not enough: gear goes past +15 towards +20, and above +15 that needs [amplify]. Don't take all dungeon gear to +20 — crafted gear (item level 94 and 102 against 86 from drops) is what is worth +20 and fine-tuned manastones.

progressionSections.titleEn: Hardcore route: enhance a cheap blank, then transfer
progressionSections.leadEn: Same steps as above, but saving every enhancement stone and kina. Depends on the datamine holding up — if transfers are limited at launch, skip this.
bullets: Enhancement cost grows with item level (Vakron Cloak, 76: 380 stones and 9,500 kina a try; Abyssal Bracelet, 84: 420 and 10,500). After +10 the chance drops (+13 → +14: 25%, +5% after each fail) and a try at the top costs about 2 million kina.
A transfer stone ([transfer_w], [transfer_a]) moves the enhancement level and rolled stats to any item — even from the cheapest gold piece to the best one. Made in Substance Morph from gold gear.

Plan: wear the lowest item level gold gear, don't enhance new drops. When a long-term upgrade drops, take a cheap blank for that slot to +15 and transfer it. Works for weapon, armor and guard, not accessories (no cheap sources).
It is slow without alts: 3–4 extra characters bring the additional enhancement stones.

progressionSections.titleEn: TitanTheF's route: Abyss farm and a crafted weapon
progressionSections.leadEn: Another route from TitanTheF's progression sheet (Taiwan experience): less waiting for dungeons, more Abyss and crafting. Needs a lot of play time.
bullets: Every Shugo Festival. Only at level 45 do you get the full rewards — including gold gear and craft materials; global also added [stigmashard]. Chests and jumping games; skip the tiles — newcomers ruin them.

Clear the map: every ? and campfire, the green side quests, and pick up hidden cubes and feathers on the way. Together with your levels that is about 316 of 570 Daevanion points (levels 136, sealed dungeons 122, regional quests 58); Shugo and Nightmare add 50 each. Feathers take the altar to level 30 and give a title.

Then one of three: kill mobs until every pet is level 3 (all pets together give 55k combat power), go to the Abyss (the same pets plus wings), or get a party for 3–4 runs of Draupnir. TitanTheF picks Draupnir — first gear, kina and enhancement.

Spend the daily Nightmare entry. One run of the first Transcendence for white arcana is enough — you only need to open floor 2. Watch the market for T1 dungeon materials and pick up everything for the season shop.
The goal of the first days: currency for a crafted T1 weapon — it is the one you will enhance and roll stats on.
At launch you won't just stand on a spot. Buy the quest scrolls from the NPC at the Abyss base — all of them, white to gold (about 1.4 million kina) — and do the white, green and blue ones.

Tag along with players doing the same quests and skip the fights — they pay less. Reroll quests towards gold materials or PvP boards, but watch the currency. Then the gold quests in the centre, then a side island to farm.

Go in pairs: two players get more AP and materials, then split the gold gear. If farming is impossible, do the same quests in the world — there is a merchant in every big city. And don't forget Shugo.
Kill every world boss once — a chance at a drop plus a participation title. The timers are on the map; there is one in almost every zone.
As soon as your item level allows, clear floor 2 of Transcendence as well (different arcana). Then Vakron and Urugugu (T2 dungeons) — watch your energy, sell what you don't need and buy T1 materials.

With enough T1 materials, level your crafting (about 2 million kina, see Gathering and crafting). Craft at least one gold level 60 blank — don't wear or enhance it. Then the T1 weapon: in the first days it should come out at no more than about 30 million kina.

Don't take the weapon above +10 yet — next are the rings (three times cheaper than weapons). Try ★3 Transcendence if energy and gear allow, otherwise kill more mobs. The solo dungeon with enhancement stones: go only for the stones, and only after raising your item level — more mobs killed, bigger reward.
Back to the Abyss: not the centre — a corner with a small pack of mobs. 8–10 hours of this gives a pile of AP, kina, gear and materials; nothing pays better in the first days.

Finish the ring, then arcana; with blue arcana and enhanced gear try the T3 dungeons. Roll stats only on T3 dungeon gear. When the energy runs out, roll the genus (about 10 million kina for all of it): don't lock stats before level 10; hidden cubes give 1,000 crystals — enough for level 10.
Don't spend unbound kina on enhancement — only on buying materials.

Later: energy into T3 dungeons, ★4 Transcendence with a good party, arcana up to level 20. After 2–3 days Abyss kills pay well; buying the necklace for Abyss points and enhancing it is fine, but not the whole Abyss set at the start — the first AP go into stigmas. Don't skip Abyss activities, weekly bosses and artifact battles — they give medals for the PvP set. Earrings can come from Kromede; the next upgrade is a crafted guard.

For those who can play 10 hours a day: Shugo as usual, the rest of the time gathering. Priority — Odyle and wood, also sapphires, rubies and diamonds; level gathering fast and forget your item level. People who know the game buy gold materials and materials in general, and crafting gets easier for you too. You can also buy kuna for kina on the auction house and flip paintings, materials and leather (cheap now, ten times more a week later). Bots are a risk here.

With 10–16 hours at launch, put the time into your main and start alts after 1–2 days, when the starting zones are emptier. With less time, take 4 characters to level 22 first and only then finish the main — by then the alts' energy is full.

progressionSections.leadEn: The five Enhancement tabs in short: Enhance, Manastone, Theostone, Soul Binding and Transfer.
bullets: Enhance. Gold gear has a 100% chance up to +10, after that it drops. A fail never breaks the item — only the materials and kina are spent. Above +15 you also need [amplify], made in Substance Morph from [amplify_frag] and [enhance].
Manastones. The number of slots depends on the rarity: white 1, green 2 and so on. There are two kinds — for weapons and armor, and for accessories — each in a normal and a PvP version ([mana_sup]).
Theostones go into the weapon and the guard: damage, damage over time or control. They trigger with a chance on attack — the higher your combat speed, the more often ([theostone]).

Soul Binding. Tab 1 raises the quality of the stats, tab 2 rerolls them — with any unneeded gold gear or reroll items — tab 3 uses books. [sync] comes from the battle pass, hard dungeons and dungeons from 2,800.
Transfer moves enhancement and stats to another item — see the hardcore route above.
Titles each give passive stats; the title info shows how to get one.
The season lasts 2–3 months. Season points buy crafting materials in the season shop.
Daily contracts (Journal → Duty → Mission) reset every day. Only the first random reward is guaranteed; the others are a chance that drops along the list — 100%, 50%, 33%, 25%, 10%.
Take every contract with the golden key in slots 1–4.
No key: short on enhancement stones — the one with the most stones; otherwise the one with the most rainbow and other pet stones.
A gold item or resource at the end of the list is almost always a trap — skip those.
💡 TIP: Hidden cubes give 1,000 crystals each — pick up every one you pass. Unbound kina is for buying materials, not for enhancement.

💡 TIP: Daily Dungeon and the trials: don't touch them and don't open their pass boxes if they are handed out at launch. They are being reworked, rewards depend on your score (kill speed), and they refresh only at the end of the week — go then, at your strongest. Weekly world and Abyss rewards are being reworked too; wait for the live numbers.
Stigmas and their levels — the biggest single jump.
Soul Binding: reroll the stats on your weapon, guard and accessories towards better ones (for example Critical Hit → Attack Speed).
Offensive items past +15 — each step adds Attack %.
Titles, Pantheon decorations (Illusion and Wisdom have the best stats) and wings — Vakron or Nightmare wings are great.
Rerolling the stats on the Pet / Genus Insight branch, and fine-tuning manastones and soulstones towards offensive stats.
Weapon skins: dismantle them on alts and use Combine on your main — every weapon you unlock adds damage with that weapon type.
